limitations: This is a local sanitized baseline, not a live production audit.
Semgrep is not installed; the repository-owned scanner applies only its documented focused rules.
No model runner is integrated; model review here is an analysis of repository source and scanner output.
No human reviewer has dispositioned findings; all dispositions are explicitly pending.
No AWS, GitHub, Docker, production, or running-container access was used.

checks.summary: Responder implementation contains no shell/process execution primitive.
Evidence base URLs are restricted to loopback hosts.
Responder output is checked against the JSON schema.
Rollback helper records authorization but executes no deployment.

findings.title: CLI operator-authorization flag is not proof of approval
findings.description: The policy CLI can label rollback as operator_authorized from a boolean argument; it does not validate an approval record. This CLI does not itself deploy, and model output validation rejects the claim, but the label can be misleading.
findings.recommendation: Remove the flag or require a verifiable operator approval artifact before emitting operator_authorized.

model_review.model_id: GPT-6 family; exact serving build unavailable
analysis: The responder implementation contains no shell, AWS, Docker, GitHub, or deployment API integration and loads no credentials. Its evidence transport is limited to fixed GET paths over loopback-only URLs, and redirects are denied.
Evidence sanitization retains only selected metric labels, three event names, and syntactically validated trace IDs; Tempo response bodies are discarded. This materially reduces telemetry exposure.

The response schema rejects additional evidence keys and the validator recomputes policy, but free-text summary and reasoning fields can still contain sensitive material if generated or copied into the result. Add content redaction checks before sharing or storing model output.

The model adapter is not implemented, so no runtime tool configuration, provider request metadata, or credentials boundary can yet be independently inspected. The current prompt specifies no tools; future integrations need an auditable no-tool configuration.

Recovery verification currently checks only local /health. It does not confirm the target deployed digest, error-rate recovery, or telemetry pipeline recovery; treat its result as a narrow health check rather than complete incident recovery.

findings.title: Free-text responder output is not content-scanned
findings.description: The JSON schema limits shape and length, but summary, reasoning, policy rationale, and escalation text can contain arbitrary strings. Schema validity alone does not prevent accidental secret or private-data inclusion.
findings.recommendation: Add a conservative output redaction/secret scan and require human review before retaining or sharing responder output.

findings.title: Loopback endpoint overrides allow arbitrary local ports
findings.description: Evidence URLs reject remote hosts and credentials, but environment overrides can target any loopback port. Fixed GET paths and redirect denial limit exposure, though a local unrelated service could receive the query.
findings.recommendation: Restrict service URLs to expected ports or use an explicitly managed local forwarding configuration with documented ownership.

findings.title: Recovery verification proves only local health response
findings.description: The recovery helper checks the local /health JSON response but does not validate the deployed version or confirm user-impact metrics have recovered.
findings.recommendation: When extending recovery verification, add read-only checks for the expected immutable version and alert recovery; keep remote/deployment credentials out of the responder.

findings.title: Model/tool provenance is not runtime-attested
findings.description: The model adapter is not integrated. Current model identity/configuration fields are documentation and audit-record values rather than runtime-attested provider metadata.
findings.recommendation: If an adapter is added, capture provider/model version, prompt/config digest, and tool capability configuration from the invoking system, then human-validate the record.
